MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 11, 2019

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Raths at 5:02 p.m., on June 11, 2019, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on June 6, 2019, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum (arrived at 5:05 p.m.)
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell
  Mayor Raths

Absent:  None

Staff Present: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6.

CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel - Anticipated Litigation; Initiation of litigation
  pursuant to paragraph (4) of subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9: 1 case.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Raths recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:05 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  1  June 11, 2019
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that CS1, the City Manager Evaluation, was continued and
the Council received an update on potential litigation issues. Direction was given but no reportable
actions occurred.

INVOCATION: Mayor Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Bucknum

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Justin Bass, MV: Asked that the City consider electrical vehicle charging stations at the civic
center.

Lance Taylor, Mission Viejo Community of Character Committee Member, M.V.: announced that
the character word for the month of June is citizenship.

Randy Johnson, MV: Stated that he is a locksmith in the Orange County area. He thanked the
Mayor for attending the Chamber breakfast and offered advisory services regarding prevention of
crime.

Elizabeth Rickett, MV: Spoke on behalf of the Canyon Democrats regarding homelessness and
the support of shelter and permanent housing facilities in South Orange County. She suggested
that the cities make a concerted effort to work together.

Mahmoud El-Farra, MV: Thanked the Council and the Quality of Life Deputy, Dana Chaney, for
their hard work. He asked the Council to work with Saddleback College and the student
government in creating on-campus student housing. He also recommended a first-time buyer
program, emergency shelters, transitional housing for the homeless, and a treaty with other South
Orange County cities so they can work together on the homeless situation.

Andrea Alexander, Lake Forest: Stated that she firmly supports a collaboration between cities that
share borders to try and find housing solutions for the homeless.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Mayor Raths, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve the Consent
Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

 1.  City Council Minutes

City Council Minutes  2  June 11, 2019
   Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of May 28, 2019, as
  presented.

 2.  Check Register Dated May 17, 2019 in the Amount of $469,201.44

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 3.  Check Register Dated May 24, 2019 in the Amount of $696,704.04

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 4.  Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo - Third Quarter 2018/19

  Received and filed.

 5.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for April 2019

  Received and filed.

 6.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for April 2019

  Received and filed.

 7.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for April 2019

  Received and filed.

 8.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for April
  2019

  Received and filed.

 9.  Community Services Funding – Fiscal Year 2018-19/ Program Cycle 2019-2020

  Approved the 18/19 Community Services Commission’s Community Services Grant
  Funding Recommendations.

 10.  Annual Routine Street Sweeping Services

  (1) Approved the Fifth Amendment with Sunset Property Services for the period of July
  1, 2019 through June 30, 2020 in the amount of $392,390.19 (2) authorized staff to issue
  a purchase order to Sunset Property Services for the period of July 1, 2019 through June
  30, 2020 in an amount not to exceed $392,390.19.

 11.  Playground, Parkland, and Facility Infrastructure Maintenance and Repair

City Council Minutes  3  June 11, 2019
   (1) Awarded a contract for (60%) of the subject services to Real Estate Consulting and
  Services, Inc.(A19-30) for the period of July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2021 in the
  amount not to exceed $504,000.00; (2) authorized issuance of a purchase order to Real
  Estate Consulting and Services, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020,
  in an amount not to exceed $252,000.00; (3) awarded a contract for (40%) of the subject
  services to Jamey Clark, Inc. (A19-31) for the period of July 1, 2019 through June 30,
  2021 in an amount not to exceed $336,000.00; and (4) authorized a purchase order to
  Jamey Clark, Inc. for the period July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020 in an amount not to
  exceed $168,000.00 pending adoption of the 2019-2021 budget by City Council.

 12.  Annual Routine Tree Trimming Contract

  (1) Approved Twenty-Sixth Amendment to the existing contract with West Coast
  Arborists, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2021 in the amount of
  $1,681,620.00; and (2) authorized issuance of a purchase order to West Coast Arborists,
  Inc. for the period of July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020, in an amount not to exceed
  $840,810.00 pending adoption of the 2017-2019 budget by City Council.

 13.  Playground, Parkland, and Facilities Safety Inspection Services

  (1) Awarded contract for the subject services to Jamey Clark, Inc. (A19-32) for the
  period of July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2021 in the amount of $665,254.80; and (2)
  authorized issuance of a purchase order to Jamey Clark, Inc. for the period of July 1,
  2019 through June 30, 2020, in an amount not to exceed $332,627.40 pending adoption
  of the 2019-2021 budget by City Council.

 14.  Janitorial and Related Services for All City Facilities and Recreation Centers

  (1) Awarded a contract for Janitorial and Related Services to Alliance Building
  Maintenance LLC (A19-33) for the period of July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2021, in an
  amount not to exceed $648,000.00; and (2) authorized issuance of a purchase order to
  Alliance Building Maintenance for the period of July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020 in
  an amount not to exceed $324,000.00 pending adoption of the 2019-21 budget by the
  City Council.

 15.  Purchase of Janitorial Related Paper, Plastic and Chemical Supplies for City
  Facilities

  Authorized Staff to issue a Purchase Order to Waxie Sanitary Supply for the period of
  July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020 in the amount of 86,000.00.

 16.  Annual Routine Park, Right-of-Way, and Facility Electrical, Lighting Maintenance
  Repair and Replacement

  (1) Awarded contract for subject services to Real Estate Consulting and Services, Inc.
  (A19-34) for the period July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2021in the amount of $522,000.00;
  and (2) authorized staff to issue a purchase order to Real Estate Consulting and Services,
  Inc. for the period July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020 in an amount not to exceed
  $261,000.00 pending adoption of the Fiscal Year 2019-2021 budget by the City Council.
City Council Minutes  4  June 11, 2019
  17.  Annual Weed Abatement Program for Parcels Under One Acre – Year 2019 –
  Phase 1

  (1) Adopted Resolution 19-12 Declaring that Certain Weeds, Rubbish, Refuse, and Dirt
  on Parcels Under One Acre Constitute Nuisances; Declaring the Intention of the City
  Council to Order the Abatement of Said Nuisances; and Fixing a Time and Place for
  Hearing Protests; (2) instructed the Public Services Department to mail a Notice to
  Destroy Weeds in accordance with Section 39566 of the Government Code; and (3)
  instructed the City Clerk to set the Public Hearing for August 27, 2019.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

 18.  Felipe Road & Oso Parkway Intersection Improvements (CIP 16224)

  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell announced that he removed this item from the Consent
  Calendar to bring to the public’s attention the effect that this project will have on
  mobility and regional transportation through the City.

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to
  authorize issuance of a purchase order for Final Engineering services for the subject
  project to Michael Baker International, Inc., in an amount not to exceed $1,268,575.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

PUBLIC HEARINGS

18.  Comprehensive User Fee Study

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Director Dyas recommended that the Council approve the fee study as is, and at future
  Council meetings some of the recommendations will be brought back for consideration.

  Mayor Raths opened the public hearing at 6:38 p.m.

  Michael Rotcher, MV: Expressed concern with the proposed termination of the fee
  waiver program for solar panel installation.

  Mayor Raths closed the Public Hearing at 6:41 p.m.

  Staff answered the Council Members’ questions.

City Council Minutes  5  June 11, 2019
   Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum to
  adopt Resolution 19-13 Amending or Augmenting the City of Mission Viejo Master Fee
  Schedule.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Kelley, and Sachs
  NOES:  Goodell and Raths
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

 20.  Lakeside Park Master Plan

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Service Keith Ratty presented the staff
  report.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelly, to
  approve the long-term master plan and conceptual design for Lakeside Park located at
  the corner of Marguerite Parkway and Alicia Parkway.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

 21.  Christopher Park Play Area Rehabilitation (CIP 312)

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Service Keith Ratty presented the staff
  report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  approve the Plans and Specifications and authorize staff to advertise for bids for the
  Christopher Park Play Area Rehabilitation.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

 22.  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Council Member Bucknum presented the report.

City Council Minutes  6  June 11, 2019
 STAFF REPORTS

 23.  Fiscal Year 2019-2020 Law Enforcement Agreement and Additional Special
  Enforcement Services Provided by the Orange County Sheriff's Department

  Emergency Operations Manager Paul Catsimanes presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Council Member Bucknum to
  (1) approve the FY 2019-20 Law Enforcement Services Agreement with the County of
  Orange (A19-35) for an amount not to exceed $19,968,791; and (2) authorize the City
  Manager to approve reimbursements related to special enforcement services in an
  amount not to exceed $35,000 for FY 2019-20.

  Council Member Sachs requested that staff write a letter to Supervisor Lisa Bartlett
  suggesting she meet with the Mayors and City Manages of contract cities to discuss the
  increased costs for the Orange County Sheriff’s Agreement and to allow for input
  during the current MOU negotiations.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

24.  Review of 2019-21 Proposed Budget

  Director of Administrative Services, Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley to (1)
  direct staff to place the 2019-21 proposed budget on the June 25, 2019 City Council
  agenda for adoption and (2) ask staff to identify possible reductions totaling $500,000
  from the FY 2020/21 budget to be presented at the next Council Meeting for discussion.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

25. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

City Council Minutes  7  June 11, 2019
 Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum asked staff for a report regarding the homeless situation at the next
Council meeting. She noted that she attended the Norman P. Murray Community Center’s 30th
Anniversary celebration and she suggested to the Council that next year they form a Relay for Life
Team and participate in the event.

Council Member Kelley

 26.  Update of Social Host Ordinance to Include Recreational Marijuana, Medical,
  Oils, Edible and Derivatives Provided to Underaged Individuals as Prohibited

  Council Member Kelley presented her report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell
  introduced Ordinance 19-329 Amending the Title of Chapter 11.22 of Title 11 of The
  Mission Viejo Municipal Code and the definition of “Controlled Substances” in Section
  11.22.010 of Chapter 11.22 Of Title 11, as Amended Providing for Accountability for
  the Host of a Gathering Where Underage Drinking or Underage Marijuana Use Occurs,
  and/or Other Controlled Substances Are Consumed.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Raths
  NOES:  Sachs
  ABSENT:  None

Council Member Kelley stated that she attended the Grapes and Grains event and the Murray
Center’s 30th Anniversary Ball and she had a great time at both. She also gave kudos to Bob Breton
for his speech about the history of the Norman P. Murray Center. Council Member Kelley said she
also attended the Capistrano Valley High School graduation and she said it was great to see such
a large number of valedictorians this year.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs cautioned seniors about scam callers portraying themselves as Social
Security Department workers. He said he called the Social Security Department and they verified
that they do not call individuals so he advised residents to be aware.

Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

Responding to an earlier comment about economic development issues, Mayor Pro Tem Goodell
announced that he spoke to Value Rock earlier in the day and he learned that there is a restriction
in their deal with Floor and Décor which limits additional space on the site to 2,800 square feet.
He said that is part of what’s driving the decision to allow a drive-through coffee and possible
restaurant adjacent to Floor and Décor. Mayor Pro Tem Goodell announced that the Swim Meet
of Champions will be held at the Marguerite Aquatics complex Thursday, June 20, through
Sunday, June 23, 2019.

City Council Minutes  8  June 11, 2019
 Mayor Raths

Mayor Raths announced the Rotary Club is hosting a breakfast at the Mission Viejo County Club
tomorrow morning from 7:00 to 8:30 a.m. He also shared that he and Council Member Kelley met
with residents in Casta del Sol to discuss their concern with the safety of the dam that faces their
community. The resident wanted to know how often the dam is inspected and City Manager
Wilberg noted that the dam is inspected annually by the State Department of Dams.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:08 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Raths adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, June 25, 2019, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, Assistant City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of June 25, 2019

City Council Minutes  9  June 11, 2019
